nationalKeyInfo.title: Value-based procurement is the national standard
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The DHSC / NHS England / NHS Supply Chain national standard scores medtech tenders on wider value (social value, efficiency, patient & staff, supply chain, purpose) weighted ≥60%, with whole-life cost capped at 40%. Procurement must save money AND show value.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Frame every case as value, not price. Build it in the Value Case Calculator and hand procurement a figure they can take to finance.

nationalKeyInfo.title: New NHS Supply Chain online catalogue
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A new online catalogue and search rolled out from late 2025 (search by NPC, MPC, supplier, brand, GTIN or free text).
nationalKeyInfo.use: A genuine, non-salesy opener: “how are you finding the new catalogue?”

nationalKeyInfo.title: New Hospital Programme reset
nationalKeyInfo.detail: Reset in Jan 2025 into delivery Waves 0–3; costed ~£56bn (NAO, Jan 2026). RAAC-affected trusts are prioritised in Wave 1.
nationalKeyInfo.use: If your trust has a new build, get in at design stage — equipment is specified 12–24 months before it opens.

nationalKeyInfo.title: Carbon scored at tender (Evergreen)
nationalKeyInfo.detail: NHS Supply Chain requires Evergreen Level 1 (a Carbon Reduction Plan + net-zero commitment) at tender close from 6 April 2026.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Have your carbon and sustainability position ready — it is scored, not optional.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NIHR HealthTech Research Centres — the NHS route to your own evidence
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A network of NIHR-funded centres of excellence hosted inside NHS trusts across England, set up specifically to help medical device, diagnostic, IVD and digital companies develop, evaluate and validate health technologies. They support real-world evidence generation and health economics, so a supplier can build NHS evidence with an NHS partner rather than arriving with vendor data alone. Each centre has its own clinical focus.
nationalKeyInfo.use: The answer when a trust says 'show me it works here'. If your evidence is manufacturer-run or from another health system, this is a named, credible route to NHS-generated proof — and raising it marks you out as someone who understands how the NHS actually accepts new technology.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NHS Supply Chain has a clinical assurance gate, not just a commercial one
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The Clinical and Product Assurance function (CaPA) sits inside NHS Supply Chain. Registered clinicians — nurses, midwives and allied health professionals — work across its clinical, commercial, customer engagement and strategy directorates to make sure the medical devices, products and consumables it sources meet NHS standards of safety, quality and effectiveness. Clinical judgement sits inside the sourcing process itself, not only at the trust that eventually buys.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Stop treating a framework as a purely commercial decision. Clinical evidence, usability and patient-safety arguments carry weight inside NHS Supply Chain's own sourcing process, not just with your trust. Ask how the clinical assurance for your category was done and what it looked at.

trusts.name: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: Queen's Hospital in Romford and King George Hospital in Goodmayes, serving one of the fastest-growing populations in England. Financially this is a turnaround account: a reported deficit of £30.7m in 2024/25 sitting on an underlying deficit of £46m, with an adjusted financial performance deficit of £38.9m against £6.1m the year before. The recovery plan requires savings of £61m, equal to 6% of income. Leadership is unusually thin on permanence — Chief Executive, Chief Operating Officer and Chief People Officer are all interim as at 14/08/2026 — so expect decisions to take longer and large commitments to need more cover than usual.
trusts.news: The Board has a Finance, Investment and Performance Committee scrutinising delivery of the financial recovery plan and savings programme, chaired by Sue Lees. The trust's own recovery narrative names right-sizing medical staffing and slippage in medical premium savings as the problems to fix, and commits to “further efficiency programmes to maintain and ensure high function performance across all core theatre capacity”. Board papers for 2026/27 are published four days before each meeting but the trust's document library does not expose them directly, so the current-year financial position could not be verified here — the £61m figure is the plan set out in the 2024/25 annual report.
trusts.structure: Payment performance has deteriorated sharply and it matters if you are carrying stock: 83.1% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume in 2024/25, down from 91.5% the year before, and 87.4% by value against 96.2%. That is the largest single-year fall in payment performance of any trust profiled in the Hub, and it is consistent with a trust managing cash through a deficit. Spend over £30,000 is published monthly. The Finance, Investment and Performance Committee is the body scrutinising the savings programme, so proposals framed as recovery-plan contributions have a named audience. Not verified: the size and structure of the procurement team, the e-tendering portal used, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published on the trust's site.

trusts.name: Barts Health NHS Trust
trusts.context: The largest trust in east London and one of the biggest in the country, with 121,464 on the waiting list but a comparatively controlled position behind it — 63.9% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 12.9 weeks and 1,095 people over 52 weeks. It has just turned a corner financially: 2025/26 closed at a surplus of £24k against the prior year's £11.7m deficit, and the trust achieved an NHS Oversight Framework rating of Segment 1 in Quarter 4. That surplus is razor-thin — a rounding error on turnover — so treat this as a trust that has fought its way to breakeven, not one with money to spare. Capital, by contrast, is substantial and rising: £173m invested in infrastructure and equipment in 2025/26, up from £118.7m.
trusts.news: Barts runs four hospitals each with its own chief executive and its own executive board — St Bartholomew's, The Royal London and Mile End, Newham, and Whipps Cross — so a trust-wide pitch has four internal customers and a site-level conversation has a named owner. A £16m Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme at Newham Hospital has entered active delivery, expected to generate recurrent energy savings of around £174k a year. The trust is also a partner in the roughly £800m Whitechapel life sciences cluster alongside private investors BGO, Lateral and H.I.G. The trust warns of “continued financial pressures in the year ahead as national reforms and system changes begin to take effect”, with emphasis on productivity, long-term workforce sustainability and accelerated adoption of digital innovation.
trusts.structure: Two things matter commercially. First, social value is measured and reported here as a procurement output, not an aspiration: over £17.15m of social value was generated through the trust's procurement system in 2025/26. A tender response that cannot evidence social value is competing badly at this trust. Second, Barts is part of the recently launched North East London Procurement Partnership, so establish early whether your category is bought by Barts alone or across the NEL sector — the answer changes the size of the prize and who you should be talking to. The annual plan and capital programme are structured to align explicitly with stated priorities, and the trust describes stronger integration between estates, facilities, clinical teams, procurement, digital and corporate functions, with sustainable procurement and supply-chain transformation named as workstreams. The audit and risk committee oversees cost improvement programmes alongside the revenue plan and capital programme. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.

trusts.name: Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A two-site trust formed by the 2020 merger of Luton and Dunstable University Hospital and Bedford Hospital, around 9,000 staff, in NHS oversight segment 3. The access position is difficult — 82,592 on the waiting list, 59.1% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 14.6 weeks and 731 people over 52 weeks. Financially it runs at the line: an adjusted financial performance surplus of £415k in 2024/25 on operating expenses of £908m, with the statutory deficit driven by the impairment of new buildings brought into use during the year. The trust has a named turnaround function that has already gone after theatre and outpatient productivity, and it says non-pay cost is the focus area for 2025/26 — which is precisely where a supplier proposition lands.
trusts.news: Pippa Nightingale has taken over as Chief Executive, arriving from London North West University Healthcare where she led the trust out of special measures and delivered financial breakeven across three acute sites; her background is as a registered midwife and she was awarded an MBE for services to nursing and midwifery leadership. The trust's Financial Turnaround Team identified 66 schemes worth £23.6m, covering theatre productivity, outpatient productivity, reducing out-of-hours operating and demand management in pathology and imaging — and the trust makes a point of having done it “on sustainable improvements rather than using external consultants”. That work has become a Strategic Financial Planning programme with a named lead. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: Procurement is held directly by the Director of Finance. Matt Gibbons's published board responsibilities are Finance, Financial Management, Procurement and Sustainability Champion — so finance, buying and the sustainability agenda sit with one person, and a case that covers all three at once is talking to a single owner. He has been in post since October 2019 and joined the organisation in 2002, so expect deep familiarity with the existing supplier base. Clinical Directors are a joint responsibility of the Medical Director and the Deputy Chief Executive, and the Medical Director, Mr Paul Tisi, explicitly owns GIRFT — a vascular and general surgeon by background, which matters if you sell into vascular or general surgery. Cathy Jones as Deputy Chief Executive holds clinical service lines, operational management, performance and business development. One stated gap worth knowing: the trust reports “a lack of a unified Electronic Patient Record system across sites” and limited interoperability with external partners, which shapes any digital or data-dependent proposition. Board correspondence goes through Victoria Parsons, Associate Director of Corporate Governance and Company Secretary, at Nova House, Luton and Dunstable University Hospital. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.

trusts.name: Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A community trust, so it files no consultant-led RTT return and carries no acute oversight segment — the data panel above will be thinner than for an acute trust, and that is correct rather than missing. Its own waiting position is comparatively good: 80.2% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 8.7 weeks and nobody over 52 weeks on a 14,961 list. The single most important fact about selling here is that BCHC does not run its own procurement. It receives procurement support on a shared basis from the BSol Procurement Collaborative, hosted by University Hospitals Birmingham, which buys for five trusts across the whole Birmingham and Solihull ICS. Win the category at BSol and you have addressed five organisations; lose it and BCHC is not a separate route back in.
trusts.news: BCHC reported a £2.6m surplus on the adjusted control-total basis for 2024/25 against a statutory deficit of £1.7m, but its cost improvement programme under-delivered — 84.5% of the year-to-date plan against a 95% target — while the capital programme over-delivered at 96.87% against a 90% target. External auditor Mazars identified no significant weaknesses in the trust's arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published on the trust's site when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated here.
trusts.structure: Procurement is delivered by the BSol Procurement Collaborative, hosted by University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust and serving UHB, Birmingham Women's and Children's, the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, Birmingham Community Healthcare and Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health — one of the first procurement teams in the country to work across an entire ICS, and winner of the HCSA 2023 Procurement and Supply Chain Team of the Year. It is led by Simon Clarke, Managing Director, whose senior management team reports into a quarterly Partnership Board and chairs the BSol Procurement Collaborative Operational Delivery Group. It holds a 'Good' CCIAF accreditation. The team is published in five parts, each with its own generic inbox, so a supplier can address the right function directly: Strategic Procurement (BSOLCategoryTeams@uhb.nhs.uk), which agrees CIP targets with finance leads, writes strategic sourcing documents for major projects and produces contract award reports; the Clinical Procurement Specialist team (ProcurementCPSTeam@uhb.nhs.uk), clinical experts reporting to a Head of Clinical Procurement who source alternatives during stockouts and national shortages and drive standardisation across the ICS; Data Analytics, Catalogue and Systems (ProcurementData@uhb.nhs.uk), which owns the BSol Master Products Catalogue — the route to getting a product code listed; Transactional Procurement (BSOLProcurementBuyers@uhb.nhs.uk), with set buyers per trust across six different ordering systems; and Pharmacy Procurement (Pharmacy.Procurement@uhb.nhs.uk). The Collaborative is based at 1 Regent Court, George Road, Edgbaston, Birmingham B15 1NU. Contracts are awarded in compliance with procurement law, trust standing financial instructions and the scheme of delegation. Not verified: whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published by BCHC or the Collaborative, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.

trusts.name: Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A mid-sized teaching trust serving around 667,000 people across seven sites, in NHS oversight segment 3, with a comparatively contained access position — 69.3% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 10.9 weeks and 55 people over 52 weeks on a 31,604 list. It beat its financial plan in 2024/25, closing a £4.9m deficit against a planned £9.7m, but the year ahead is much harder: a projected £17m deficit for 2025/26 requiring £33m of productivity savings. The opening is capital rather than revenue — three named new-build schemes are in flight, and all three are directly relevant to devices and consumables.
trusts.news: The trust names three new capital developments as live opportunities to improve services: a new Community Diagnostic Centre, a dedicated day case unit at St Luke's Hospital, and a new endoscopy suite. Financial governance runs through a programme the trust calls 'Closing the Gap', alongside development of an Estates Strategy and prioritisation of backlog maintenance. Internal audit during the year covered Estates Procurement (BH48 2024) and Procurement and Business Cases (BH25 2025), so procurement process is under active internal scrutiny. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: Procurement is unambiguously a finance function here. The trust's own table of executive directors' key responsibilities puts Finance, Procurement, Contracting and Capital all under the Chief Finance Officer — so the CFO is the accountable owner of a buying decision, not a distant approver, and a business case that reads as a finance case will travel further than one that reads as a clinical wish. Estates, the Capital Programme, Clinical Engineering and Sustainability sit together under the Director of Estates and Facilities, which is the route for equipment, maintenance and backlog cases. The trust also works with West Yorkshire partners on joint projects spanning procurement, so check whether a category is bought at West Yorkshire level before assuming it is a Bradford decision. One observable quirk worth knowing: five of the seventeen Bradford buyer contacts in the Hub's own contacts data were named on notices whose title begins 'Waiver' — single-tender waivers published as award notices — and no other trust in this batch shows any. That is counted over published notice titles only, and it is a signal about how contracts here get published, not proof of how they get awarded. Not verified: no e-tendering portal, procurement team structure or supplier representative booking system is confirmed — the trust's public website is behind bot protection and could not be read directly, so none of this could be checked on the live site.

trusts.context: The largest clinical supplies buyer in this batch by a wide margin — £418m a year, more than Leeds, Nottingham and Birmingham put together — and the largest waiting list of any trust in the Hub directory. trusts.name: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: Hull is the most pressured elective performer in this batch. The waiting list stands at 84,186 with only 56.8% treated within 18 weeks, the worst figure of the batch against a constitutional standard of 92%, a median wait of 15.1 weeks and 3,188 patients waiting over 52 weeks. The trust sits in NHS oversight segment 4, the mandated-support tier, and reported 6 Never Events and 63 cases of C. difficile. High-risk backlog maintenance is carried at £16,847,256. For a rep, that combination is the classic elective-recovery and estate-risk opening: capacity, throughput, theatre and diagnostic productivity, and infection prevention all have a named problem attached to them here. But segment 4 also means every spending decision is visible to NHS England, so anything pitched has to be argued on activity delivered or cost released, not on preference.
trusts.news: The 2024/25 annual report, signed on 20/06/2025, carries an external auditor's exception report naming a significant weakness in the trust's arrangements for financial sustainability. The auditors found the trust set a deficit plan, reported a year-end surplus only because it received deficit support funding, and did not fully deliver a cost improvement programme that leaned heavily on non-recurrent savings, all of which increased the cumulative deficit. They also record that as at April 2025 the trust had not identified all the savings needed for its 2025/26 CIP target and that a significant level of that CIP was rated high risk. Separately, the report confirms the trust opened Community Diagnostic Centres in Grimsby and Scunthorpe, expected to deliver up to 300,000 additional diagnostic tests a year, with a further centre in Hull opening in summer 2025 and the final phase of the Day Surgery Unit and the Allam Centre for digestive diseases and endoscopy coming online at Castle Hill Hospital. The Capital and Major Projects Committees-in-Common agenda for 2024/25 included an EPR business case review, the Community Diagnostic Centre developments and the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme.
trusts.structure: The group arrangement is CONFIRMED by the trust's own site, not inferred. www.hey.nhs.uk/about-us/our-senior-team/ now returns a 301 permanent redirect to the Northern Lincolnshire and Goole board page, and www.hey.nhs.uk/about-us/corporate-documents/ points its annual reports link to the same NLaG domain, where the reports for both trusts are published jointly under the name NHS Humber Health Partnership. That shared board page states in its own words that NLaG and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust 'operate under a Group model of leadership' with 'one, shared, executive team but two separate boards, overseen by a Group Chairman'. The 2024/25 HUTH annual report says the same from the trust's side: it joined with NLaG in August 2023 in a new group structure with a Group Chief Executive and group executive team, the group name NHS Humber Health Partnership was formally launched in spring 2024, and joint clinical services across both trusts, called care groups, were formed at the same time and split into north and south site management. Commercially this is the single most important fact about Hull. You are not selling to one trust with its own executive; you are selling to a shared executive team that buys for two trusts, meets as Boards-in-Common and Committees-in-Common, and holds procurement, capital and cost improvement at group level via the Performance, Estates and Finance Committees-in-Common. Procurement goes further still. Hull is the HOST organisation for the Humber and North Yorkshire Procurement Collaborative, described on its own page as 'a single procurement function covering three local NHS Trusts' - Hull, NLaG and York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust - employing 119 staff and managing an annual influenceable non-pay spend of £538m, governed by a Procurement Board accountable to all three trust boards. A supplier winning at Hull is therefore potentially transacting across three trusts, and the buying contacts sit in a shared team rather than in Hull alone. trusts.name: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute and specialist trusts in England, running St Mary's, Charing Cross, Hammersmith, Queen Charlotte's & Chelsea and the Western Eye hospitals, with total income of £2,029.7m in 2025-26. Waiting list 83,936 with 70.6% treated within 18 weeks, a median wait of 10.7 weeks and only 28 patients waiting over 52 weeks — a large but comparatively well-controlled list. NHS oversight segment 1, the best band, so this is not a trust under special measures and its leadership has headroom to make its own decisions rather than having them made by a regional turnaround team. Against that, 5 Never Events and 70 cases of C. difficile. The single dominant commercial fact is a high-risk backlog maintenance liability of £446,418,142, by far the largest in this batch. The trust's own 2025-26 accounts put that in the going-concern note, stating the estate's condition is a significant risk and that failures would be 'unaffordable for the Trust to rectify within its own resources'. Three main sites were pushed into Wave 3 of the New Hospital Programme in January 2025, with construction not expected between 2035 and 2038, so the ageing estate has to be kept running for another decade on revenue and small capital allocations.
trusts.news: Big governance change in 2026. The North West London Acute Provider Group was formally established on 01/04/2026, bringing Imperial together with Chelsea and Westminster, London North West University Healthcare and The Hillingdon Hospitals under a single accountable officer, a chair in common and a board in common — 12 hospitals, 33,000 staff, a population of around 2.2 million. Professor Tim Orchard, previously Imperial's chief executive, became the first Group chief executive and single accountable officer on 01/04/2026, and Professor Julian Redhead stepped up as Imperial's trust chief executive from the same date, announced on an interim basis for at least 12 months. Bob Alexander OBE has been interim chair in common since 01/04/2026; on 28/07/2026 the trust announced Dame Alwen Williams, formerly group chief executive of Barts Health, as the permanent chair, taking up the role on 01/11/2026. Commissioning also changed: NHS West and North London ICB was created on 01/04/2026 from the merger of North West London and North Central London ICBs, covering over 4.5 million people across 13 boroughs, and around 58 per cent of Imperial's income comes from it. In May 2025 there was a fire at St Mary's Hospital requiring remedial works, and reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC) was found in the outpatients building at St Mary's, with feasibility assessments funded in the 2025-26 capital programme.
trusts.structure: Imperial does NOT run its own standalone procurement function. Its Standing Financial Instructions define the term explicitly: 'Procurement or the Procurement service refers to North West London Procurement, who now provide procurement support to the Trust as part of a shared service to the NWL sector.' That is the single most important thing for a supplier to know — a rep who pitches a clinician at Charing Cross and assumes a local Imperial buying decision will follow is working the wrong route. The chief financial officer, Jazz Thind, owns the relationship with that shared service and is responsible for holding it to account; competitive tender and quotation thresholds sit in the Trust's Scheme of Delegated Financial Authority, and single tender waivers must be approved by the Procurement Service, the CFO or the chief executive, with all waivers reported to the Audit, Risk and Governance Committee. So the trust buys through a sector shared service, not for itself and not as a host buying for others. On top of that, the 2025-26 annual report states the trust is 'seeing the benefits from sector-wide procurement and management of digital services, both of which create efficiencies that are shared across north west London', and non-pay procurement improvements were one of the named contributors to the £80.1m efficiency target. The trust also co-chairs a north west London-wide social and sustainable procurement working group, and states that social value and net zero principles are embedded in its procurement processes — expect those weightings in tender scoring. Clinical leadership is unusually concentrated: there are TWO medical directors (Professor Raymond Anakwe, and Dr David O'Callaghan who holds quality, safety and clinical governance), three clinical divisions each with its own director reporting to the chief operating officer, and Professor Bob Klaber OBE holds strategy, research and innovation — the natural door for anything positioned as innovation or a research partnership. Not verified: the exact competitive tender and quotation monetary thresholds. The Standing Financial Instructions repeatedly point to the Scheme of Delegated Financial Authority for the actual figures, and that schedule is not published alongside the SFIs on the trust website. An FOI request to the trust, or a request to North West London Procurement, would settle it. Not verified: whether the formation of the North West London Acute Provider Group on 01/04/2026 has changed the procurement operating model beyond the shared-service arrangement described in the SFIs. The published Standing Financial Instructions carry an adoption date of March 2022 (version 7.0) with a stated review deadline of March 2025 for the Executive and March 2026 for the Audit, Risk and Governance Committee, so the document may pre-date the Group. It does cite a January 2024 policy, indicating some in-life updating, but a rep should confirm the current arrangement directly rather than assume. Not verified: whether North West London Procurement holds a published supplier portal or contracts register — no such page was found on the trust's own site during this session; the trust publishes only monthly expenditure-over-£25,000 CSV returns.

trusts.name: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute trusts in England, running Denmark Hill, Princess Royal University Hospital, Orpington and Beckenham Beacon, with national specialist services in liver, neurosciences, haemato-oncology and cardiac care. The elective account is very big and under strain: a waiting list of 89,923, with 67.5% treated within 18 weeks against the 92% standard, 1,708 patients waiting over 52 weeks and a median wait of 11.6 weeks. The Trust sits at segment 3 of the NHS Oversight Framework, having exited segment 4 in April 2026 and come off NHS England's Recovery Support Programme. Infection control is a live pressure with 93 C. difficile cases, and there is £1,216,386 of high-risk backlog maintenance on the estate. For a rep, this is a trust with enormous volume, genuine specialist prestige, and a finance function under explicit regulatory scrutiny, so nothing gets bought on clinical enthusiasm alone.
trusts.news: The 2025/26 Annual Report and Accounts were published in July 2026 and show the group returning a surplus of £10.837m, a control-total surplus of £4.951m after adjusting for impairments and donated assets. The Trust confirms it exited NHS England's National Oversight Framework segment 4 in April 2026 and was removed from the Recovery Support Programme, which the Chief Executive frames as evidence of recovery rather than completion. Against that, the July 2026 public Board pack reports the King's group (the Trust plus KFM and KCS) £1.8m in deficit year to date at May 2026, and an underlying deficit of £18.0m once non-recurrent items are stripped out. Four Care Quality Commission service inspection reports published during 2025/26 found the Trust's improvements were not universal. Matthew Trainer is Chief Executive; search engines still return a previous post-holder, and the Trust's own executive directors page confirms the current line-up.
trusts.structure: The single most important structural fact for anyone selling to King's is that the Trust does not run its own procurement. The Trust's own support services page states that "Procurement activity is managed by King's Facilities Management (KFM) on behalf of the Trust, following best commercial practice and public procurement regulations." KFM is King's Facilities Management LLP, a Trust-owned entity created to run nine diagnostic and treatment facilities (theatres, adult critical care, radiology, cardiac catheter laboratories, liver laboratories, endoscopy, renal dialysis, children's critical care and dental), maintaining the equipment and supplying the consumables, implants and devices used in those procedures. Separately from the managed-facilities contract, the 2025/26 Annual Report states KFM "provides an end-to-end procurement and supply chain function for the Trust" and is explicitly tasked with delivering cost improvement programme savings through more focused contract management. KFM has also run the outpatient pharmacy service on the Trust's behalf since 2019. So the answer to the buy-for-itself, shared-service or buy-for-others question is: all three at once. KFM buys for King's, and KFM's own procurement and supply chain page markets end-to-end procurement, supply chain and logistics to "King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and a growing healthcare client base" beyond it. A supplier relationship built at KFM is therefore potentially a route into other clients, not just this trust. Practically, suppliers must register on the Atamis eProcurement system to bid, opportunities are advertised on Contracts Finder and the Find a Tender Service as well as through Atamis, and the Trust states the commercial procurement pipeline is published on the KFM website. Cold-calling a clinician at Denmark Hill will not get a purchase order; the route is Atamis registration plus the KFM pipeline. Two other Trust-owned companies matter commercially: King's Commercial Services Limited, which returned a £0.7m surplus to the Trust in 2025/26 and owns the Trust's stake in the Synnovis LLP pathology joint venture (so pathology buying sits inside Synnovis, not the Trust), and KCH Management Limited, which runs hospital management and consultancy overseas, mainly in the Middle East, returning £0.1m. The Trust is also part of a South East London Acute Provider Collaborative with Guy's and St Thomas' and Lewisham and Greenwich, established in May 2020 and building specialty-based elective hubs across the patch, so high-volume low-complexity elective capacity decisions are being taken at collaborative level rather than by King's alone. Not verified: the size of KFM's addressable procurement spend as distinct from the Trust's total non-pay spend, and the identity of KFM's procurement director or category leads. Neither is disclosed in the Annual Report or the July 2026 Board pack. A Freedom of Information request to the Trust, or KFM's own Companies House filings, would settle the first; the second would be settled by KFM's published pipeline or a direct approach through Atamis. Not verified: which named individuals hold category ownership for medical devices or consumables. Not verified: whether the reported KFM contract extension to 2036 that appears in secondary coverage is accurate; it does not appear in the 2025/26 Annual Report or the July 2026 Board pack read for this profile, and only a Trust or KFM primary source or a published contract award notice would settle it.

trusts.name: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute providers in England: around 20,000 staff, four main hospital sites (Salford Royal, The Royal Oldham, Fairfield General, Rochdale Infirmary) and roughly 2,000 beds, serving over a million people across Salford, Oldham, Bury and Rochdale. Operating income for 2024/25 was £2,013,226k. The elective position is severe and is the headline commercial opening: a waiting list of 133,771, only 57.2% treated within 18 weeks, a median wait of 15.2 weeks, and 3,608 patients waiting over 52 weeks - the highest 52-week breach count in this batch. Quality and infection metrics are also under pressure: 9 Never Events and 132 C. difficile cases. High-risk backlog maintenance stands at £3,369,731. The trust sits in NHS oversight segment 4 (mandated intensive support), which means external scrutiny of spend and a hard bias towards anything that demonstrably reduces cost or shortens a pathway. Note the trust's own 2024/25 Annual Report, published earlier, states it was then in Segment 3 - the segment 4 position is the later, current one.
trusts.news: On 06/08/2026 the trust announced that Salford Royal had joined a Greater Manchester roll-out of an AI prostate cancer detection tool, a pilot led by Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance also running at Wigan, Bolton and Stockport. The tool analyses prostate MRI scans and flags those most likely to show cancer so radiologists can prioritise the highest-risk men. Mr Sotonye Tolofari, consultant urological surgeon at Salford Royal, is quoted leading the trust's involvement. Commercially this tells a rep two things: NCA is willing to be an early site for diagnostic technology, and the buying decision for that class of product ran through the Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance rather than the trust alone - so a system-level route can matter as much as the trust route. Separately, the 2024/25 Annual Report records that an outline business case was developed during 2024/25 to procure and implement an NCA-wide electronic patient record, with a formal programme team established and a data cleanse and electronic document management workstream under way. Any product that needs to integrate with the EPR should expect that programme to gate it.
trusts.structure:
The trust is organised into five Care Organisations - Salford, Bury, Rochdale, Oldham, and a trust-wide Diagnostics and Pharmacy Care Organisation covering pathology, pharmacy and radiology across all four hospital sites. This is the single most important structural fact for a rep. Each Care Organisation has, as a minimum, its own Chief Officer, Director of Operations, Medical Director, Director of Nursing, Finance Director and Human Resources Director (2024/25 Annual Report, 'Care Organisations', pp.4-7). A trust-wide pitch therefore has at least five internal customers with their own operational leadership, sitting under one corporate board and one set of shared corporate services. Salford Royal carries the specialist weight: the Manchester Centre for Clinical Neurosciences (neurosurgery, neurology, stroke, spinal surgery) and the Greater Manchester Major Trauma Hospital, which opened on 07/05/2024. Royal Oldham has vascular surgery, urology, gynaecology, a trauma unit and a level three maternity unit. Rochdale Infirmary hosts a GIRFT-accredited elective day case surgical hub serving the whole trust - the natural target for elective recovery products. Bury (Fairfield General) covers A&E, elective surgery, ENT and a specialist stroke unit. On the trust's public website the section is now titled 'Our Hospitals', though the URL still reads 'our-care-organisations'.

Pharmacy is run as a trust-wide group service with named, publicly listed contacts (page last updated 03/07/2026): Lindsay Harper as NCA Group Director of Pharmacy, Gavin Leahy as Interim Director of Pharmacy, plus Heads of Pharmacy, Principal Pharmacists and Chief Pharmacy Technicians per site. The Head of Pharmacy post at Royal Oldham is listed as vacant. There are four inpatient dispensaries, one per site. Outpatient dispensing at Royal Oldham and Salford Royal is contracted out to Rowlands Pharmacy; Fairfield General and Rochdale dispense outpatients in-house. Two aseptic services units, at Salford Royal and Royal Oldham, prepare cytotoxic chemotherapy, antibiotics, clinical trial products and parenteral nutrition.

Procurement: the trust runs its own in-house procurement department. The 2024/25 Annual Report ('Procurement and Supply Chain', pp.46-47) states that the majority of the department's senior team are CIPS qualified, many recently upgraded to chartered status, and that the department also uses central framework contract providers and runs a supplier relationship management process with regular contract and supplier meetings. Bidders must evidence Modern Slavery Act compliance under PPN 03/23, and the trust has adopted the Social Value Model from PPN 06/20, applying a minimum 10% weighting in all procurements to net zero and social value - so a bid that ignores social value is losing a tenth of the score before it starts. Procurements from 17/02/2025 fall under the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024.

Not verified: whether NCA buys through a Greater Manchester system-level or shared procurement service, or provides procurement services for other organisations. No public procurement, suppliers or e-tendering page could be found on the trust website, and the Annual Report describes an in-house department without naming a shared service. The trust does act as host for other NHS bodies - notably Advancing Quality Alliance (AQuA), £5,044k of hosted income in 2024/25 - but that is a hosted service, not a buying arrangement. This would be settled by a Freedom of Information request to the trust, or by the trust publishing a supplier/tenders page.

The board page lists only the corporate board; the Annual Report confirms the roles exist but does not name the current post-holders in the section read. A board paper listing Care Organisation leadership, or an FOI request, would settle it.

Also relevant but not among the six named below: Lorna Allan is Chief Digital and Information Officer (joined September 2022) and is the natural first contact for anything touching the EPR programme; Gertie Nic Philib is Chief People and Strategy Officer; Sheena McDonnell is Chair and Professor Chris Harrison is Non-Executive Director and Vice Chair, appointed vice chair in November 2025. trusts.news: Month 2 (May 2026) reported to the public Board on 09/07/2026: £23.0m year-to-date deficit, £6.1m adverse to plan, with a £4.5m year-to-date overspend on clinical supplies and services driven by higher-than-planned activity. The National Rehabilitation Centre, a 70-bed purpose-built NHS facility near Loughborough and the first of its kind in the UK, is staffed and run by NUH and due to open.
trusts.structure: NUH operates a strict “no purchase order, no payment” policy — an invoice without an official PO number, and not on the exception list, is rejected outright. The PO is issued before you start supplying and is emailed to the address held in your supplier record, so get your supplier details right before anything ships. Invoices go to NHS Shared Business Services, not to the trust; accountspayable@nuh.nhs.uk handles disputes. They aim to pay within 30 days and frequently do not: in 2024/25 only 59.9% of non-NHS invoices were paid on time by volume and 58.4% by value, so price your working capital accordingly. Contracts over £25k are published on Contracts Finder. The distinctive route in for a device company is CHEATA — the Centre for Healthcare Equipment and Technology Adoption, a contract-based service embedded in the trust's Clinical Engineering department offering value propositions, health economic analysis, evidence gathering, NICE engagement and regulatory advice to manufacturers at any stage. trusts.context: A mental health, learning disability and community trust, so it files no consultant-led RTT return and carries no acute oversight segment — the data panel above will be thin, and that is correct rather than missing. Two things make it unusual. It is lead provider for three NHS provider collaboratives — forensic inpatient mental health, CAMHS Tier 4 and adult eating disorders — holding the budgets and commissioner responsibilities for those specialised services, so it buys as a commissioner as well as a provider. And it runs the Oxford Pharmacy Store, a trading service that grew by £28m in the year.

She came from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, where she was also Chief Finance Officer, with earlier senior civil service finance roles at HMRC, BIS and HM Treasury — expect a public-sector business-case discipline rather than an NHS-only frame of reference. trusts.name: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest teaching trusts in England, running the John Radcliffe, Churchill, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre and Horton General. Layer-1 verified position: 90,534 patients on the waiting list, 62.5% treated within 18 weeks, median wait 13.3 weeks and 1,713 waiting over 52 weeks. NHS oversight segment 3. Seven Never Events and 107 cases of C. difficile. High-risk backlog maintenance stands at £54,815,755, which is the single biggest structural story here: the trust's own annual report shows only circa £6.5m spent in 2024/25 on estates compliance and backlog maintenance combined, so the gap between the liability and the annual spend is roughly eight to one. Financially the trust reported a control-total deficit of £6.8m for 2024/25 against a planned position, but the underlying deficit (one-off items stripped out) is estimated at £77m, a deterioration of about 20% on the £61.3m underlying deficit a year earlier. It sits within the Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West (BOB) Integrated Care System, which was placed into the national Investigation and Intervention regime during 2024/25 after the system-wide position deteriorated.
trusts.news: The chief executive seat is not settled. Professor Meghana Pandit remains the substantive Chief Executive Officer but has been on secondment to NHS England since 01/04/2025, first as Co-National Medical Director - Secondary Care and, from 01/04/2026, as a Deputy Chief Executive Officer to Sir Jim Mackey, splitting her time 50/50 between OUH and the national role. Simon Crowther took up the post of Acting Chief Executive Officer on 01/04/2025 and was appointed Interim Chief Executive Officer in September 2025 for the remainder of the secondment. Sir Andrew Morris OBE began a fresh term as Chair on 01/08/2026. The board has also refreshed heavily: Lynne Graham joined as a Non-Executive Director on 01/04/2026 and Kenny Kamal on 01/01/2026. Separately, the trust reset its procurement authorisation limits: a board paper taken in public on 11/03/2026 revised contract ratification thresholds upwards, moving the point at which a contract needs Trust Board sign-off from £500,000 to £3,000,000 for goods and services.
trusts.structure: OUH buys for itself. It runs an in-house Procurement and Supply Chain Team under a Director of Procurement and Supply Chain, with a published strategy organised around five areas: Strategic Sourcing - Divisional Procurement / Medical Technology; Strategic Sourcing - Corporate and Non-clinical; Supply Chain Transformation; Commercial and Contract Management; and Innovation and efficiency. There is a single published route in for suppliers: ProcurementandSuppliesQueries@ouh.nhs.uk. The function is not a shared service and the trust's own Standing Financial Instructions place procurement authority internally, with the Director of Procurement and Supply Chain ratifying all contracts up to the published UK regulatory limit. Note the split of a dedicated medical technology sourcing team from corporate/non-clinical sourcing - a device rep should be aiming at the former. The trust does host bodies for others, but the hosting named in the Standing Financial Instructions is the Thames Valley and Surrey Secure Data Environment, a data platform, not a procurement shared service. Not verified: the name of the current Director of Procurement and Supply Chain. The board directors page does not list the role (it is not a board-level post) and the published organisational structure chart does not name it; a direct enquiry to the procurement mailbox, or a recent procurement-related board paper naming the postholder, would settle it. Not verified: whether OUH and Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust operate any joint or shared procurement arrangement. The annual report confirms the two trusts work together at Place level within the Oxfordshire system and share governor-level links, but neither the OUH procurement page nor the Standing Financial Instructions describes any shared buying function, and Find a Tender notices carrying @ouh.nhs.uk addresses for Oxfordshire-wide services were not read in this session. Reading the specific Find a Tender notices, or the OUH Procurement and Supply Chain Strategy document itself, would settle who contracts for what. Not verified: the identity of the Chief Strategy Officer beyond the interim - Jay Mistry is listed as Interim Chief Strategy Officer with no substantive appointment shown.

trusts.context: A £1.76bn teaching trust across the Royal Hallamshire, Northern General, Weston Park, Charles Clifford and Jessop Wing, and one of the few in this batch that is genuinely in surplus — £6.93m, 0.4% of turnover, on turnover up 11.5%. That makes it a different sell from the turnaround trusts: they are not desperate, so a pure price argument carries less weight, and the trust says plainly that 2025/26 brings “an even more constrained financial position”. Their stated approach is driving out unnecessary variation rather than blanket cuts, which favours suppliers who can evidence standardisation and reduced variation over those offering a discount.
trusts.news: Clinical supplies spend rose more than a fifth in a year, to £164.3m. The trust has almost eliminated the longest waits for treatment while its waiting list grew 0.7%. Its stated priorities for the year are “driving out unnecessary variation, refining our ways of working and through partnerships explore how we deliver the best value for the resources we are given”, navigated as a partner in the wider South Yorkshire system rather than alone.
trusts.structure: Two published procurement commitments are directly actionable for a supplier. First, social value is a part of all competitive procurements and environmental considerations are built into procurement processes — so it is scored, not decorative. Second, and more unusually, the procurement teams are explicitly working to increase the use of local businesses and suppliers specifically to reduce the road miles in their supply chain and support the local economy. If you have a Yorkshire or northern distribution point, warehouse or manufacturing site, that is a scoring argument here and not merely a nice story — quantify the road miles saved. Note the trust runs two Chief Medical Officers, split into Development and Operations, so the right clinical sponsor depends on whether you are proposing a new service or improving an existing one. trusts.news: The chief executive position is split. Sir James Mackey remains substantively chief executive but is on secondment to NHS England, and Rob Harrison is acting chief executive covering that secondment; the trust's own live board page still showed this arrangement when read on 15/08/2026 (https://www.newcastle-hospitals.nhs.uk/about/board-of-directors-2/board-of-directors/). trusts.structure: Procurement is run in-house, not through a shared service and not outsourced. The chief finance officer, Jackie Bilcliff, carries "supplies and procurement" as an explicit named responsibility in her board biography in the 2024/25 annual report, and the trust refers throughout to "our Procurement Team". Its own sustainable procurement page puts annual spend at over £700 million across around 4,000 supply chain companies. The single most important thing for a supplier to know is the gate: it is mandatory for every active tier 1 (direct) supplier to submit carbon data annually by the end of June via a published five-step framework, to register on the SmartCarbon platform using the trust's supplier code NUTHSUPP10, to publish a 2040 net zero commitment, and to publish a carbon reduction plan meeting at least the PPN 006 government template. Social value and net zero are stated as embedded in the procurement strategy, policy and tender processes. Purchased goods and services account for over 85% of the trust's total carbon footprint, so this is a live scoring criterion rather than a formality. Newcastle also sells services outward through a separate commercial arm at commercial.newcastle-hospitals.nhs.uk, with named lines including the North East Innovation Lab, Newcastle Hospitals Biobank, Novopath, Newcastle Hospitals Laboratories, Newcastle Specials (pharmacy production unit), Newcastle Advanced Therapies, the National Centre for Neurotechnology and Neurorestoration, occupational health and data partnerships. It also hosts regional infrastructure on behalf of the North East and North Cumbria ICS, specifically the Great North Care Record shared care record and the Connect NENC digital referral platform launched in November 2024, and hosts the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Laboratory Hub contract, which brought in an additional £31 million of income. The 2024/25 report flags clinical supplies as a pressure area, noting medical devices moving onto block funding and more items moving onto the visible cost model - a rep should expect device spend to be scrutinised line by line. Not verified: whether Newcastle procures on behalf of any other trust or hosts a formal collaborative procurement function for the region. The annual report and the trust's public procurement pages say only that the trust "collaborates with other NHS trusts and public sector peers to align approaches", which is not the same as buying for them. trusts.context: Do not sell to this trust as a standalone organisation. ULTH and Lincolnshire Community Health Services NHS Trust operate as the Lincolnshire Community and Hospitals NHS Group, and the Group Board is “the joint board and decision-making body for both statutory organisations” — a single set of group executives covers finance, operations, estates and clinical governance across both. It sits in NHS oversight segment 4 and stayed there at the Quarter 4 2025/26 ratings published in June 2026, with a 70,206 waiting list, 61.9% within 18 weeks and 1,113 people over 52 weeks. The commercial picture is not simply distress, though: the trust over-delivered its savings plan in 2024/25 and fully spent an £88.1m capital programme, and has an unusually visible pipeline of new-build diagnostic and theatre capacity.
trusts.news: The Group Board meeting of 07/07/2026 reported an £8.1m deficit at month two, in line with plan, and confirmed ULTH remained in oversight segment 4 at the Quarter 4 National Oversight Framework ratings while LCHS dropped from segment 2 to 3. The ULTH Electronic Patient Record implementation is “continuing at pace”, with first go-live scheduled for October 2026 and parallel digitisation of existing paper records. The Lincolnshire Community Diagnostic Centre programme now runs CDCs at Grantham, Skegness and Lincoln with a fourth being built at Boston. The Lincolnshire system formally exited Urgent and Emergency Care Tier 2 oversight in May 2026. Implementation of the new Patient Services Hub has been temporarily paused while problems are worked through. Capital is governed through a Capital Delivery Group reporting to the Finance, Performance and Estates Committee, with quarterly reporting, and the capital prioritisation process is informed by the six-facet estate survey — a backlog-maintenance case has a defined route here. Estates is the standout capital relationship: Group Chief Estates and Facilities Officer Mike Parkhill has run the largest capital programme in the trust's history, covering the Lincoln County emergency department, urgent treatment centre and respiratory support unit, new theatres at Grantham, the Grantham CDC, the new Pilgrim emergency department and the Lincoln and Skegness CDCs. trusts.name: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: The strongest financial position in this batch and the only segment 1 trust in it — a £17m surplus in 2025/26 and £329m of cash at 31 March 2026. It is also the best performer on access here: 65.0% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 11.9 weeks and 884 people over 52 weeks on a 77,531 list. That combination makes it a capital play rather than a cost-cutting one. But read the outlook before assuming an easy year: the trust calls 2026/27 “extremely challenging” and faces a recurrent savings requirement of £92.6m to break even, which it describes as “an unprecedented level of challenge”. Its commissioner also changed on 01/04/2026, when North Central London ICB merged with North West London to form West and North London ICB.
trusts.news: UCLH was chosen by the Department of Health and Social Care as the launch site for its programme to cut reliance on single-use items, with the minister shown reusable and remanufactured theatre products in a mock theatre on site — reusables, remanufacture and Design for Life are live procurement priorities here, not aspirations. The trust is also leading the procurement and commissioning of a PACS shared in common across North Central London hospitals, and a national first-in-type scheme integrating Epic with the national e-prescription service, due to let patients collect UCLH prescriptions from community pharmacies in 2027.
trusts.structure: Procurement sits under Tim Jaggard, deputy chief executive and chief financial officer, who signed the 2025/26 accounts on 25/06/2026. Sustainability is an explicit and published part of buying decisions: the trust commits to “ensure sustainability forms a greater part of our procurement decision-making”, to “meet or exceed NHS England's procurement roadmap”, to increase reuse and remanufacture while reducing single-use, and to engage suppliers to pilot more sustainable items. Supply-chain emissions are the largest part of a 202,818 tCO₂e carbon footprint, with net zero for indirect and supply-chain emissions targeted by 2040. The trust uses NHS Terms and Conditions and weighs modern slavery factors in procurement decisions. It pays well by NHS standards — 91% of invoices by volume and 96% by value paid to terms in 2025/26. Several large buys run at North Central London level rather than trust level, PACS being the current example, so check whether your category is bought by UCLH alone before targeting it. trusts.name: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Four hospitals — Queen Elizabeth Birmingham, Heartlands, Good Hope and Solihull — and one of the largest trusts in England. Financially it is under formal NHS England scrutiny: the trust reported an overall deficit of £69.5m in 2024/25 and, on the adjusted measure NHS England judges it on, a £0.9m surplus reached only after a Financial Recovery Plan agreed in September 2024 in response to an £81.4m adjusted deficit at month eight. It is rated 4 — Investigation and Intervention — under the NHSE Rapid Intervention process. The savings that got them there do not repeat: over half were non-recurrent, so the same gap reopens each year. A trust that needs recurrent, provable savings, not one-offs.
trusts.news: The 2024/25 accounts record control weaknesses that delayed the draft accounts and the audit, causing the trust to miss the national timetable. Clinical supplies spend rose to £251.3m. No 2026/27 board papers were publicly locatable on the trust's website as at 14/08/2026 — unlike Leeds and Nottingham, UHB does not publish an accessible board pack archive, so the current-year position here is not verified. Ask your contact directly rather than assuming the 2024/25 picture still holds.
trusts.structure: UHB does not buy only for itself. It hosts the BSol Procurement Collaborative, which provides procurement and supply chain services across the Birmingham and Solihull ICS to five trusts: UHB, Birmingham Women's and Children's, the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, Birmingham Community Healthcare, and Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health. Win a category here and you have addressed five organisations at once; equally, the other four are not separate ways back in if you lose it. The Collaborative is led by Simon Clarke, Managing Director, whose senior management team reports into a quarterly Partnership Board, chairs the BSol Procurement Collaborative Operational Delivery Group, and approves significant contracts and major projects. UHB describes it as one of the first procurement teams to work across an entire ICS, winner of the HCSA 2023 Procurement and Supply Chain Team of the Year, and holder of a 'Good' CCIAF procurement standards accreditation. Five teams are published, each with its own inbox, so a supplier can approach the right function directly: Strategic Procurement (BSOLCategoryTeams@uhb.nhs.uk), which agrees CIP targets with finance leads and produces strategic sourcing documents and contract award reports; the Clinical Procurement Specialist team (ProcurementCPSTeam@uhb.nhs.uk), clinical experts reporting to a Head of Clinical Procurement who source alternatives during stockouts and national shortages and drive standardisation across the ICS; Data Analytics, Catalogue and Systems (ProcurementData@uhb.nhs.uk), which owns the BSol Master Products Catalogue and is therefore the route to getting a product code listed at all; Transactional Procurement (BSOLProcurementBuyers@uhb.nhs.uk), with set buyers per trust across six different ordering systems; and Pharmacy Procurement (Pharmacy.Procurement@uhb.nhs.uk and BuyingOfficePharmacy@uhb.nhs.uk). UHB's own procurement page was last reviewed 05/09/2024, so confirm the named post-holder is still in place before using it. Unusually, each of the four hospitals has its own Hospital Executive Director sitting outside the main Board — Matt Metcalfe (Queen Elizabeth), Dr Rifat Rashid (Heartlands), Simon Jarvis (Good Hope) and Martin Richardson (Solihull). That matters for targeting: a site-level conversation has a named owner, and a trust-wide pitch has four internal customers, not one. Efficiency is benchmarked through the national Reference Cost Index, GIRFT and Model Hospital data, and the trust says this is shared with the hospital sites for planning — so GIRFT and Model Hospital comparators are the language that lands here. Payment performance is mid-range: 76.9% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume, 73.4% by value in 2024/25. Not verified whether UHB runs a rep booking or accreditation system, or which e-tendering portal it uses.

trusts.name: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: One of the larger acute trusts in the Midlands, with group income of £1,351.887m and an average of 13,890 whole-time-equivalent staff in 2024/25. Operationally it is under pressure: a waiting list of 96,379 with only 61.4% treated within 18 weeks, a median wait of 13.4 weeks and 1,782 patients waiting over 52 weeks. It sits in NHS oversight segment 4 (mandated support), the most intensive tier, which means NHS England is directly involved in its recovery. Quality signals are mixed: 5 Never Events and 131 cases of C. difficile in the period. Estate risk is material, with £14,683,291 of high-risk backlog maintenance outstanding. For a supplier, the commercially important point is that segment 4 status and a 5% efficiency requirement mean every proposition has to be framed around cost release, productivity or waiting-list throughput, not incremental clinical preference.
trusts.news: The trust's own news feed through 2026 has been dominated by productivity and digital stories rather than capital expansion. In May 2026 it reported a national award for a digital system credited with getting patients faster care, over 11,000 patients receiving faster care through staff-led improvement, a further boost to on-site solar power, and recognition for use of the CareScan tool. Also in May 2026 CQC rated Derby and Burton services 'Good'. Earlier in the year the reported innovations were clinical-pathway ones: home phototherapy sleeping bags for babies with jaundice (June 2026) and innovative voice therapy for Parkinson's Disease (April 2026). In the 2024/25 year the trust opened a new centre at Royal Derby Hospital after £10m of construction and a £5.1m facility including an Open MRI scanner described as one of only two of its kind. Source: https://www.uhdb.nhs.uk/latest-news/ and the 2024/25 Annual Report and Accounts.
trusts.structure: The single most valuable structural fact is that UHDB is not only a buyer for itself, it is a host of procurement for others. The trust hosts the East Midlands Pharmacy Collaborative (EMPC), described on its own page as 'a small dynamic procurement team providing a Pharmacy procurement service for its member Trusts', covering twelve member trusts: Chesterfield Royal Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust, Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Leicester Partnership NHS Trust, Northampton General Hospital NHS Trust, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust, United Lincolnshire Hospitals NHS Trust, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust and Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust. For a pharma supplier this means a single tendering route at UHDB can reach twelve trusts across the East Midlands, and that losing at UHDB can mean losing far more than one trust's volume. UHDB is also part of Joined Up Care Derbyshire, the system within which its control total and deficit support were agreed. Non-pharmacy procurement (medical and surgical equipment, dressings, laboratory) appears from the annual report to run as the trust's own function, with spend reported by eClass category. Live board titles were taken from the trust's own board page on 15/08/2026 and supersede the annual report, which still lists Andrew Hall as Executive Chief Operating Officer and Debbie Loke as Executive Chief Digital Information Officer; the live page now shows Paran Govender and Andy Carruthers in those roles. Searches restricted to uhdb.nhs.uk returned no procurement or tenders page, and guessed URLs on this site 404 rather than redirect. This would be settled by a Find a Tender or Contracts Finder search on the trust's buyer profile, or by contacting the trust directly. Not verified: whether UHDB belongs to a wider non-pharmacy shared procurement service or NHS Supply Chain hosted arrangement beyond EMPC; nothing on the trust's own site states this either way. Not verified: the named head of procurement or chief pharmacist, neither of whom appears on the board page. Not verified: any 2025/26 in-year financial position; the newest published accounts are 2024/25, and no 2025/26 figures should be presented as current.

trusts.name: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute trusts in the country and, on the numbers, one of the hardest-pressed in this batch: 115,259 on the waiting list, 60.1% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 14.0 weeks, 2,402 people over 52 weeks, and NHS oversight segment 4. It is also a serious deliverer of savings — £69.4m of cost improvement in 2024/25, after £64.2m, £35m and £17.1m in the three years before — but it has never yet hit the ask, and the 2025/26 target is £92m. Capital is large and consistent, running at £75m to £122m a year. The trust's own stated goal for the year is blunt: “Reduce pay and non-pay costs by £92m.” A proposition that cuts non-pay cost recurrently is aimed directly at a published target here.
trusts.news: For 2025/26 the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland system plan forecasts an £80m deficit, of which UHL accounts for £65m, on an assumed £92m cost improvement programme — and the trust states plainly that “long term financial sustainability is dependent upon CIP improvements being delivered recurrently”. The New Hospital Programme investment at UHL has been deferred by up to three years, leaving only £1.5m of previously committed NHP funding in the 2025/26 capital allocation. Several executives now hold 'Group' titles — Group Chief Nurse, Group Chief Digital Information Officer — so confirm whether a decision in your category is UHL's alone or made across a wider group before targeting it. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: The most useful thing UHL publishes is its list of senior clinical leaders by service line, which gives a named clinical director for most device-relevant specialities without any need to guess: Chris Allsager for Critical Care, Theatres, Anaesthesia, Pain and Sleep; Monika Kaushik for Musculoskeletal and Specialist Surgery; Kate Hodgson for Cancer, Haematology, Urology, Gastroenterology and General Surgery; Rob Davies for Renal, Respiratory and Cardiovascular; Prashanth Patel for Clinical Screening and Imaging; Jonathan Cusack for Women's and Children's; and Neeta Patel for Emergency and Specialist Medicine. That is the clinical champion, and the trust names them itself. Sustainability is a formal part of buying: the trust has implemented carbon reduction requirements for new procurements, formed a Sustainable Procurement Working Group, and secured representation at LLR system level, with Supply Chain and Procurement run as one of its named sustainability workstreams. It pays suppliers well, at 93% against the Better Payments Practice Code. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site. Note also that Find a Tender notices are frequently published against a single central inbox (uhl-tr.uhlprocurementopportunities@nhs.net) rather than a named buyer's own address, so the contacts panel above will often route to a team rather than an individual.

trusts.name: University Hospitals of North Midlands NHS Trust
trusts.context: A £1.29bn-income trust across Royal Stoke University Hospital and County Hospital in Stafford, with around 1,450 inpatient beds, in NHS oversight segment 3. The access position is mid-table for this batch — 72,002 waiting, 63.0% within 18 weeks, a median wait of 13.1 weeks, 1,360 people over 52 weeks. The fact that shapes every commercial conversation here is the Section 30 referral: because of a cumulative deficit, the trust's external auditors referred it to the Secretary of State for Health in June 2021, and that referral was still in place through 2024/25. Expect scrutiny of any spend, and expect recurrent savings to be valued far above one-off ones — the trust says its 2024/25 position “relied heavily on non-recurrent cost improvement scheme delivery and other one-off benefits”.
trusts.news: The trust ended 2024/25 with an £11.8m deficit against a breakeven plan and has appointed a Recovery Director alongside a revised Urgent and Emergency Care improvement programme. Its County Elective Hub has significantly increased procedure numbers, with day case activity running at 107.4% of plan — the elective hub is the growth point. On the supply side, the Procurement Team's Energy Procurement Partnership with Stoke-on-Trent City Council cut a potential £10m cost pressure to around £3m and has been extended for a further two years, and the second and final phase of the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme put £3m into air source heat pumps, LED lighting and solar at Royal Stoke as part of a £5.4m programme. Not verified: the 2025/26 annual report and accounts had not been published when this profile was written, so no current-year outturn is stated.
trusts.structure: The most useful thing to know about this procurement team is that it co-develops products with suppliers rather than only buying them. Its published example is the Eco Box, developed jointly with the trust's anti-embolism stockings supplier: they removed the dye to save energy, water and chemicals, stripped the plastic packaging, trialled it on wards, and then adapted the format again after patients said they preferred individually wrapped take-home packs — projected saving 7.8 tonnes of plastic and 10 tonnes of cardboard a year. A supplier arriving with a sustainability redesign proposal has a proven precedent to point at. Procurement also sits inside the monthly Sustainability Working Group structure, and the team runs supplier awareness work on Modern Slavery Act compliance as part of onboarding new suppliers, so expect that check when trading for the first time. Financial performance, cost improvement schemes and capital schemes are all standing monthly items at the non-executive-led Performance and Finance Committee, which is where a large business case will be seen. Estates, Facilities and PFI are held together by one director, and the trust describes “exemplar relationships” with its PFI partners. Not verified: no e-tendering portal or supplier representative booking system is published on the trust's public site, and not publishing one is not proof there isn't one.
